simple.meaning: נָהַק (nâhaq) is a Hebrew action word meaning “to bray (as an ass), scream (from hunger).” BibleIQ anchors the English reading to this source verb before comparing its uses.
simple.biblicalBackground: This action appears 2 times in Job, beginning at Job 6:5. Its meaning becomes clearer as the uses are compared.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to נָהַק (H5101) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Actions in Scripture show what people do, what God does, and how covenant faithfulness or rebellion is described. BibleIQ compares the action across its occurrences.
simple.summary: נָהַק (nâhaq) / H5101 is traced through Job 6:5, Job 30:7 with source-language evidence and verse context.
